solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Proof that mother knows best when it comes to remedies?

definitions.text: Proof that mother knows best when it comes to remedies?

parts.words: Proof that mother knows best when it comes to remedies?
parts.note: the mother is Mother Nature, and healing left to her own ways is a treatment named after her

explanation.surface: A homely claim that mum's home remedies beat anything the doctor offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' reads as a parent, but it is Mother Nature, whose way of healing gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Healing by natural means such as diet and rest is the remedy system Mother Nature would vouch for.

clue.text: First, second, third or fifth letter in 'money'?

definitions.text: First, second, third or fifth letter in 'money'?

parts.words: First, second, third or fifth letter in 'money'?
parts.note: the tonic, second, third and fifth of a scale are musical pitches each named by a letter A to G, and a piece of paper currency is also meant

explanation.surface: A puzzle about spelling: which letters of the word money are meant?
explanation.walkthrough: Positions in money seem meant, but these are degrees of a musical scale, each named by a letter, and the same word is a piece of paper currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical pitch is named by a letter A to G, and paper currency such as a fiver goes by the same word.

clue.text: 'Leaves much to be desired' would be praise from him

definitions.text: 'Leaves much to be desired' would be praise from him

parts.words: 'Leaves much to be desired' would be praise from him
parts.note: the leaves are tea leaves, so someone grading tea would call a fine blend leaves much desired

explanation.surface: A critic whose usual put-down would count as a compliment.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means disappointing, but for a professional judge of tea, leaves very desirable are high praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional who samples and grades tea leaves would value leaves that are much desired.

clue.text: Levers top off and defies gravity

indicators.note: top off says the first letter of the word for levers is removed

parts.note: prises means levers open

explanation.surface: Prising a lid off something that then floats upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes up rather than falling is ascending, so it seems to defy gravity.

clue.text: Worked on shoe when horse got hurt

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
bled means lost blood, got hurt

explanation.surface: A farrier shoeing a horse that was injured in the process.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes, so shoes he has mended have been repaired in this way.

clue.text: They attack, at rear end, those helping

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of rear

parts.note: aiders are people who aid or help

explanation.surface: Assailants attack the helpers from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: People who make sudden attacks are assailants or invaders, a noun plural in both.

clue.text: Drag from said building

indicators.note: said signals that the word for the building is spoken, and its sound is what we enter

parts.note: a hall is a large building or room

explanation.surface: Something being dragged out of a building, as if a removal team were at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something heavy along is to pull it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Island makes a charge for drivers

parts.note: a toll is a fee for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: An island authority makes motorists pay a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral ring enclosing a lagoon is a kind of island.

clue.text: What a shortfall in the US may lead to?

definitions.text: What a shortfall in the US may lead to?

parts.words: What a shortfall in the US may lead to?
parts.note: in America fall is autumn, so a short autumn means the cold season comes early and lasts

explanation.surface: An economist's question about the effects of an American shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortfall reads as a deficit, but in American English fall is autumn; a short one leaves more of the year to the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: If autumn is short, the cold season that follows must be extended.

clue.text: Public transport one way, fly back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for fly is read from its end to its start

parts.note: fly in the slang sense of sharp or clever means smart

explanation.surface: Directions for a passenger: take the bus or train out, then fly home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way' hints that the answer read in one direction is the transport and in the other is the word for fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are street railway cars running on rails, a form of public transport in many cities.

clue.text: Creates condensation in the kitchen

parts.note: condensation suggests steamy windows, but here it is a sauce being reduced by heat in a pan

explanation.surface: A steamy kitchen with water running down the windows.
explanation.walkthrough: Condensation is taken as concentrating: a cook reduces a liquid by heating it so it thickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Reducing a liquid by heat condenses it, and figuratively summarises something to its essence.

clue.text: Person artist's painting is not the Queen

definitions.text: Person artist's painting is not the Queen

parts.words: Person artist's painting is not the Queen
parts.note: a person under a monarch's rule rather than the monarch, and also the topic an artist paints

explanation.surface: A portrait painter's sitter turns out not to be the monarch after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses run together: what a painting depicts, and a citizen ruled by a sovereign rather than the sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen owing allegiance to a monarch is one, and so is the thing a painting depicts.

clue.text: Forgive mariner having illicit loves

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: illicit suggests the loves are improper, here meaning their letters are put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A sailor with affairs in every port is being let off by his partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon someone is to release them from blame or guilt, which is what forgiving does.

clue.text: Shout 'Reduced by fifty, it's down'

indicators.note: reduced by tells us something is taken away from the shout

parts.note: to bellow is to shout loudly
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A headline-style shout that a price has been cut by fifty and has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifty looks like a percentage cut, but it is the Roman numeral L removed from BELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Down and beneath both mean in a lower position, so one replaces the other.

clue.text: Dangerous moment, shutting the lunatic inside

indicators.note: inside says the scrambled word goes within the word for shutting

parts.note: closing means shutting

indicators.note: lunatic suggests crazy, so the letters of the are scrambled

explanation.surface: A near-disaster while locking up a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shutting' looks like part of the scene, but it supplies the outer word; 'lunatic' is the anagram signal, not a description of the inmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape or near miss is a risky moment when disaster almost happened.

clue.text: Secured mislaid chalet key

indicators.note: mislaid suggests something put in the wrong place, so the letters of chalet are rearranged

parts.note: D is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone lost the key to the holiday chalet, but the door was locked.
explanation.walkthrough: Key reads as a door key, but it is the musical key D.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is fastened by a catch is secured, the past tense matching.

clue.text: Didn't allow to spout freely

parts.note: spout here means to make a speech, and interrupting with jeers stops a speaker doing so

explanation.surface: Something that prevented a fountain or pipe from flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spout suggests a pipe, but it is a speaker holding forth, interrupted by a hostile audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrupting a speaker with jeers and barracking stops them speaking without hindrance.

clue.text: Sheathing little gun to pacify

indicators.note: sheathing means enclosing, so the gun wraps round the little word

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Putting a small gun away in its holster to calm a tense situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone more agreeable by softening the deal is to mollify or placate them.

clue.text: So three got off with a warning

indicators.note: got off suggests escaping, here meaning the letters of three get out of order

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout

explanation.surface: Three people escaped with only a caution, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Fore is the shout golfers give to warn people in the ball's path.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a consequence, as in 'I think, so I am'.

clue.text: 'Wind Damaged Most Of Corsica' — Globe

indicators.note: damaged suggests something broken, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
most of says the final letter of the island's name is dropped

parts.note: a globe is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline reporting a storm that wrecked most of a Mediterranean island, from a paper called the Globe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe looks like the newspaper's name, but its shape gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot Saharan wind that blows across the Mediterranean, including over Corsica.

clue.text: Dump a flood damaged figurehead stored therein

indicators.note: stored therein says the letter goes inside the reordered letters
damaged signals the letters of a flood are broken up and reordered

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of figure

explanation.surface: A ship's figurehead, kept in a store, is thrown out after flood damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns A FLOOD into OFLOAD, with F 'stored therein'.
explanation.definitionFit: To get rid of something unwanted is to unload it, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Seen in context, remedies going too far

indicators.note: seen in signals the answer can be spotted spelt out within the next words

explanation.surface: A warning that, taken in context, certain remedies are overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken to excess is beyond reasonable limits, so the adjective fits going too far.

clue.text: Mixing a rum with half of bitter — awful mistake

indicators.note: mixing drinks suggests stirring together, so these letters are combined in a new order
half of takes the latter three letters of bitter

explanation.surface: A barman's awful error: mixing rum with a half of bitter beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives TER from bitter, mixed with A RUM; 'awful' is surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An error in printing or writing, listed in a correction slip, is a mistake.

clue.text: Child alone missing one is what it amounts to

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: missing says the word for one is taken out of alone

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child left alone is the sum of the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: The sum that everything adds up to is what it amounts to.

clue.text: Questions time taken over jobs

indicators.note: taken over places the letter for time before the word for questions in a down answer

parts.note: asks means questions as a verb

explanation.surface: Interrogations take up time that should go on work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of work to be done are duties or chores, plural like jobs.

clue.text: Why did the Japanese go to the bar? (Give up?)

definitions.text: Why did the Japanese go to the bar?
definitions.meaning: a riddle whose reply is that they went for the rice wine of Japan
to give up is to abandon or renounce

explanation.surface: A cracker joke: the setter asks why a Japanese visitor went to the pub, then asks whether you give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The rice wine saké gives the punchline 'for saké', which sounds like the word for abandoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon or renounce is to forsake, as in forsaking all others.

clue.text: On the other hand, it's just what a slimmer doesn't want

definitions.meaning: used to introduce a contrasting point

definitions.text: it's just what a slimmer doesn't want
definitions.meaning: a dieter wants no increase in weight, read as two words

explanation.surface: Then again, it's the very thing a dieter dreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Then again or besides introduces a counterpoint; split as two words it is weight put on.

clue.text: Instrument that's really played without heart

indicators.note: played suggests performance, here meaning the letters are freely rearranged
without heart drops the two middle letters of really

explanation.surface: An instrument that was really played without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without heart' takes AL from REALLY, and 'played' rearranges RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: The harp-like stringed instrument of ancient Greece is an instrument.

clue.text: Thoroughly showing what bowlers try to get

definitions.meaning: knowing something completely, in every detail
in cricket the fielding side's bowlers try to dismiss the batting side, getting those in out

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: displaying in full detail the aim of every bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in'; bowlers try to get that side out.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing a subject in every detail is knowing it completely; and getting the batsmen in out is the bowlers' aim.

clue.text: Any attempt to inject is painful

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective, while the answer is the noun for great pain

indicators.note: to inject means putting something inside, so the attempt goes into any

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Any attempt at giving an injection hurts, says a nervous patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the adjective stands for the noun, suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense physical or mental suffering is what something painful brings.

clue.text: Have trouble breathing — that's when doctor's brought round

indicators.note: brought round says the doctor is placed around the word for when

parts.note: GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A patient struggles to breathe, and the doctor is called to revive them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' suggests reviving a patient, but it signals the doctor going round AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle for breath is to pant or draw air in sharply, a verb of the same kind.

clue.text: First two fallers in the race

definitions.text: First two fallers in the race

parts.words: First two fallers in the race
parts.note: the race is the human race, and the fall is the Fall of Man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A horse-racing report: the first two horses to tumble in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: Race reads as a horse race, but it is mankind, whose first couple fell from grace in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first humans were the first to sin and be cast out, the first of humankind to fall.
